lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Best Buy
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 7, Session 2
lesson.footer: Money and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 2

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09) with Year 5 (VC2M5N07): modelling purchasing decisions by comparing unit prices with division, interpreting and justifying the choice
plan.shape: problem-first: two packs of muesli bars with different sizes; students guess the better buy before the teacher models the unit price
plan.criticalFeature: compare the price of the same amount: one item, 100 g or 1 L
decisionPoints: the choice check: 6 for $9 or 4 for $5?
the hinge: 2 L for $5 or 3 L for $6.60?
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Show one sale price worked out on a bar model, then start at the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it
Under it: unit price = price divided by how many

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Unit prices, which pack is the best buy, a mistake to fix, and canteen and sports store problems.
resources.title: Best Buy
resources.subtitle: Compare the price of the same amount.

example.prompt: 8 muesli bars cost $6. What does one cost?
steps: Divide the price by how many: $6 divided by 8.

items.prompt: Find the price of one item in each pack.
Which pack of footy cards is the best buy?
items.explain: 50c, 60c and 55c each: 10 for $5 is cheapest per card.

items.prompt: Which bottle of water is better value?
items.explain: Per 100 mL: 30c and 24c. The 1.5 L bottle is better value.

items.prompt: Tom says the 12-pack is cheaper because $9 is less than $10. Find his mistake and fix it.
work: $9 is less, so the 12-pack is the better buy.
items.answer: Compare one can: 12 for $9 is 75c each, 20 for $10 is 50c each. The 20-pack is the better buy.

example.prompt: Is it cheaper to buy 2 packs of 3 balls at $12 a pack, or 6 balls at $3.50 each?

items.prompt: The canteen sells muffins at $2.50 each or a box of 6 for $12. How much do you save on 6 muffins with the box?
A team needs 24 drink bottles. Packs of 4 cost $14 and packs of 6 cost $19.80. Which packs should they buy, and how much will it cost?
items.answer: Packs of 4: $3.50 each, 6 packs = $84. Packs of 6: $3.30 each, 4 packs = $79.20. Buy packs of 6: $79.20.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Unit prices per 100 g, when the bigger pack is not better, and a multi-buy deal, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Smart Shopper
resources.subtitle: Not always the biggest pack.

example.prompt: 500 g of rice for $3.50. Price per 100 g?

items.prompt: Find the price per 100 g, then circle the best value.
Which is better value: 1 kg of apples for $4.50, or 750 g for $3.60? Show the price per 100 g.
items.answer: 1 kg: 45c per 100 g. 750 g: 48c per 100 g. The 1 kg bag is better value.

items.prompt: A 2 kg bag of dog food costs $11. How much should a 5 kg bag cost to be the same value?

example.prompt: Why might you buy the smaller pack even if it costs more per item?
steps: Food can go off before you finish it.
example.answer: if you won't use it all

items.prompt: A family needs 6 eggs this week. A 12-pack is $6 and a 6-pack is $3.90. Which should they buy? Explain.
items.answer: The 6-pack ($3.90): the 12-pack is cheaper per egg (50c) but costs more and they only need 6.

items.prompt: Make up a situation where the bigger pack is the worse choice.
items.answer: For example: fruit that goes off, or a big tub of paint for a tiny job.

example.prompt: 'Buy 2, get 1 free' on $4 drinks. Price for 3?

items.prompt: Shop A: 'Buy 3, get 1 free' on $5 socks. Shop B: '25% off' $5 socks. You need 8 pairs. Which shop is cheaper? Show your working.
items.answer: Shop A: pay for 6 pairs = $30. Shop B: 8 × $3.75 = $30. They are the same.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: easy divisions, a step frame, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Best Buy: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Price for one = price divided by how many.

items.hint: Find the price for one in each.
Find the price for one in each.

slides.notes: Session 2 of our money and percentages fortnight: today we find the best buy.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk; calculators are optional for checking. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Missing side
prompts: Area 128 m², one side 8 m. Other side?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with area, perimeter and division.
ASK: How long is the other side?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 16 m
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> say 8 times what is 128, then divide with the bracket. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 128 divided by 8 is 16 metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 120, by subtracting.
Fix: say 8 times what makes 128, and they divide.
notes.prep: Review of Week 5 area and perimeter (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is the area of this L-shape?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 64 m²
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> draw the split line, find each rectangle, add. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The bottom is 11 by 4, which is 44,
and the top is 5 by 4, which is 20.
44 plus 20 is 64 square metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: multiplying the two longest sides.
Fix: shade the missing corner, and they split it.

slides.title: Perimeter
prompts: A square paddock has a perimeter of 84 m. How long is each side?

beats: ASK: How long is each side of the paddock?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 21 m
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> say a square has 4 equal sides, then divide by 4. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 84 divided by 4 is 21 metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 42, by halving.
Fix: say 4 equal sides, and they divide by 4.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some short division with the division bracket.
Divide each digit from the left, and carry any remainder across.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 135
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 135.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.
notes.prep: Division fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 791
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 791.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7 932
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 7 932.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to compare prices to find the best buy.
successCriteria: I can find the price of one item in a pack.
I can compare unit prices to find the best buy.
I can explain when the best buy is not the best choice.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we worked out sale prices.
Today we work out which deal is really the best value.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 price for one is reachable for everyone; SC2 comparing unit prices is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 judging the choice is the stretch.

slides.title: Which pack?
slides.prompt: Which pack is the better buy?

beats: POINT to both packs.
SAY: Two packs of muesli bars. One has more bars, but it also costs more.
ASK: Which pack do you think is the better buy?
Show one finger for the 6-pack, two for the 4-pack.
10 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: a mix
MODEL dividing each price.
SAY: Let's check one bar each.
9 dollars shared by 6 is 1.50, and 5 dollars shared by 4 is 1.25.
SAY: So the smaller pack is the better buy here.
Today we learn to compare the price of the same amount, every time.
trap: choosing the 6-pack because it has more.
Fix: find the price of one bar in each, and they compare again.
notes.prep: Problem-first: a guess before the unit price. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: The price of one item, or one unit like 1 kg or 100 g.
slides.example: 8 bars for $6 is a unit price of 75c a bar.

beats: POINT to the words.
SAY: These words are unit price. Say them with me: u-nit price.
SAY: The unit price is the price of one, like one bar or 100 grams.
Shops print it on the shelf label so you can compare.
ASK: 4 apples cost $2. What is the unit price of one apple?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 50c
trap: writing $8.
Fix: say price divided by how many, and they divide.
notes.prep: Unit price makes different-sized packs comparable.

beats: POINT to the division.
SAY: 5 drinks cost 7 dollars 50.
To find one, I divide the price by 5.
MODEL the division bracket.
SAY: 5 into 7 is 1, remainder 2.
5 into 25 is 5. 5 into 0 is 0.
So one drink is 1 dollar 50.
ASK: 6 drinks cost $8.40. What is the unit price?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $1.40
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 8.40 divided by 6 is 1.40: 1 dollar 40 each.
trap: dividing 6 by 8.40.
Fix: say the price is shared out, and they set it up again.
notes.stretch: How much would 15 drinks cost at that price?
notes.help: Change dollars to cents first: 840c divided by 6.
notes.prep: Unit price = price divided by how many. SC1.

answers: 2 L for $3: 15c per 100 mL, best of all

beats: POINT to the juice sizes.
SAY: When the sizes are different, I compare the same amount. I'll use 100 millilitres.
MODEL each unit price.
SAY: 1 litre is 10 lots of 100 mL,
so 2.40 divided by 10 is 24 cents.
750 mL works out at 28 cents, so the litre is better value.
ASK: A 2 L bottle costs $3. What is its price per 100 mL?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 15c
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 2 L is 20 lots of 100 mL,
and 3 dollars divided by 20 is 15 cents.
trap: comparing the total prices.
Fix: ask whether the bottles are the same size, and they find the unit price.
notes.stretch: What price would make 750 mL match?
notes.help: Count the lots of 100 mL first.
notes.prep: The critical feature: compare the price of the same amount. SC2.

options.misconception: chooses the bigger pack without checking the unit price

beats: SAY: Find the price of one in each pack first.
ASK: Which is the better buy: 6 for 9 dollars, or 4 for 5 dollars?
20 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What is each unit price?
Less -> divide each price on the board together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B. 6 for 9 dollars is 1.50 each,
and 4 for 5 dollars is 1.25 each.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: find the price of one in each, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A means bigger is assumed better.

slides.title: Find the unit price
slides.ask: What is the price for one?
slides.pivot: change to cents, then divide with the bracket
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How did you check it?

items.say: 10 for 7 dollars is 70c each, cheaper than 75c.

say: Write each unit price on your board.
trap: dividing how many by the price.
Fix: say the price is shared out, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Find the price of 15 of each.
notes.prep: Guided practice: easy divisions, cents, per kilogram, then a comparison. SC1 and SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Compare the price of one litre.
ASK: Which milk is better value, and what is its price per litre?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3 L, $2.20 a litre
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> divide each price by the litres together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 2 L is 2.50 a litre, and 3 L is 2.20 a litre.
So the 3 L bottle is better value. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing 2 L because $5 is cheaper.
Fix: ask what one litre costs in each, and they compare.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone choosing the 2 L starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Find unit prices and best buys on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Are you comparing the same amount?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: comparing total prices.
Fix: find the price for one, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: price per 100 g, when bigger is worse, and multi-buy deals.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: easy divisions and a step frame.
notes.prep: Independent practice: unit prices, best buys, a mistake and real problems. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Which pack of socks is the better buy? Show the price per pair.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: Which pack of socks is the better buy,
and what does one pair cost in each?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 5 pairs: $3.20 vs $3.50
RECORD who compares totals or divides the wrong way.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: choosing 3 pairs because $10.50 is less.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new comparison with decimal unit prices.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how to find the best buy.

notes.answer: open - listen for work out the price for one of each, then compare
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can find the best buy?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with '3 pairs' on the board matters most.
ASK: How do you find the best buy?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: work out the price for one of each, then compare
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: when prices go up.
